subject.title: fix(discord): sustained gateway bursts stop growing memory

question: Should ordinary Discord Gateway presence/member sends intentionally use the new drop-oldest policy during a sustained one-window backlog, or should a different owner-level retention policy be adopted?
rationale: The code and tests establish a concrete policy, but choosing which non-critical Gateway state updates may be discarded during overload is an operational delivery contract that requires maintainer intent.

options.title: Accept newest-state retention
options.body: Keep the bounded drop-oldest queue after reviewing live saturation proof because stale ordinary state updates are less useful than the newest desired state.

options.title: Choose a different overload contract
options.body: Specify a caller classification or coalescing policy before merge if some ordinary Gateway events must never be discarded.

recommendation.title: Accept newest-state retention
recommendation.body: Keep the bounded drop-oldest queue after reviewing live saturation proof because stale ordinary state updates are less useful than the newest desired state.

likelyOwner.reason: He authored the final overload-policy and warning revisions and is the clearest available routing candidate.
